import { Aside, Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

This template names every invoice by what is printed on it: the vendor, the invoice date, the invoice number, and optionally the amount. It works on born-digital PDFs and on scanner output — image-only scans are read with AI vision.

## Naming pattern

```
{Detected Date} – {Vendor} – {Invoice Number} – {Amount}
```

| Block | Source | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detected Date | The invoice date printed in the document (not the file date) | `2026-06-12` |
| Vendor | The issuing company, normalized to one spelling | `Acme Supply` |
| Invoice Number | Exactly as printed, prefix included | `INV-10234` |
| Amount | Total with currency code — optional but useful for reconciliation | `1,204 USD` |

## Before and after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| `download (7).pdf` | `2026-06-12 – Acme Supply – INV-10234 – 1,204 USD.pdf` |
| `Scan0001.pdf` | `2026-06-03 – Cloudflare – CF-88112 – 96 USD.pdf` |
| `invoice_copy.pdf` | `2026-05-28 – Rippling – RIP-2026-1180 – 4,830 USD.pdf` |

## Build it

<Steps>
1. Open **Templates** in the sidebar and create a new Template named "Invoices".
2. In the naming pattern, add the **Detected Date**, **Vendor**, **Invoice Number**, and **Amount** [Naming Blocks](/docs/naming-blocks); set the date format to `YYYY-MM-DD`.
3. Optional: add a [Custom AI Block](/docs/custom-ai-blocks) for an expense category — describe your category list ("Software, Travel, Meals, Hardware") and the AI assigns one per invoice.
4. Run a test batch of 10–20 mixed invoices, review the preview, and adjust block order or separators.
5. Assign the Template to [folder monitoring](/docs/folder-monitoring) on the folder where invoices land.
</Steps>

<Aside type="tip">
Invoices without a printed number (common for small vendors) simply leave the block empty — date plus vendor plus amount is almost always unique. The preview catches the rare collision.
</Aside>
